Direct substitution verifies budget equality, positivity and an increasing generalized four-block path eigenvector at B/F. The Sturm ordering of the irreducible path and two leaf-difference spectra establish lambda2=B/F. Equality in the same upper certificate determines each individual optimizer weight uniquely; the left/right polygon constructions remain valid for a or b=2 and at boundaries. Exact-rational verifier passed 368 cases (including all principal minors of the quotient spectral lower bound); these checks supplement rather than replace the proof.

originality.rationale: The paper proves a closed and unique three-price/three-phase optimal allocation for proper double stars, including cost-induced Fiedler multiplicity transitions. The 2006 primary paper states the general cost-weighted FMMP SDP and embedding dual and solves weighted paths, but does not give the double-star formula. The 2014 primary full text derives uniform-price double-broom formulas and its equal-price specializations are prior art; it does not vary three price classes. Actual research-record queries returned unrelated Laplacian, double-star zero-forcing, and bistar-polytope results, not a statement entailing the new optimizer. Residual implicit coverage in specialist tree-embedding literature remains possible.
residual_risks: An implicit special case of a more general theorem about cost-weighted tree embeddings may reproduce the three-price formula without the same naming.
Full text of Fiedler (1990) was not accessible; only its publisher abstract and relevant later citations were available.
Research-record and web search cannot certify absolute publication priority.

value.rationale: The spectral-gap optimum under distinct conductor procurement costs across two leaf classes and a connecting bridge has a direct network-design interpretation. The theorem completely identifies the rate, unique individualized allocation, and two price-driven eigenvalue-multiplicity boundaries for a natural infinite tree family, beyond a generic SDP or a uniform-price table. It also explains the geometric switch from a one-dimensional optimum to a saturated hub with transverse leaf spread.
